claims.text: The initial (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has poor integrity and tends to crack.
Thermomechanical processing can refine the grain size of the alloy.
Thermomechanical processing can produce an optimized crystallographic texture in the alloy.
Refined grains and optimized texture will enhance grain-boundary cohesion.
Refined grains and optimized texture will reduce crack propagation.
Reduced crack propagation and enhanced grain-boundary cohesion will improve the alloy's integrity.
The intervention will increase compressive strength by at least 20% relative to the unchanged alloy.
A 20% strength improvement corresponds to a treated-alloy compressive strength of 183 MPa.
The intervention will maintain the caloric response within 10% of that of the unchanged alloy.
The predicted benefits apply from 250 K to 350 K.
The predicted benefits apply under magnetic fields up to 5 T.
The predicted benefits apply under pressure fields up to 100 MPa.
A controlled comparison against the unchanged alloy can test the effects of varying grain refinement and texture-control parameters on strength, caloric response, and microstructure.
The hypothesis is to be falsified if strength increases by less than 15% or caloric response decreases by more than 15% relative to the unchanged alloy.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 20% strength increase, but the experiment only falsifies increases below 15%; therefore a 15–20% increase would fail the prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.

The prediction requires caloric response to remain within 10% of baseline, whereas falsification occurs only for a decrease greater than 15%; a decrease between 10% and 15% violates the prediction but is not declared falsifying.
